patterns.name: Always Validate API Key Format
patterns.description: Validate API key format at application startup to prevent runtime authentication errors. Ensures keys follow expected patterns (e.g., 'sk-' prefix for OpenAI) and provides clear error messages with remediation steps.
best_practices: Validate API keys during application initialization, not at first use
Provide clear error messages with links to credential management
Use environment variable validation libraries like zod or joi
Log validation failures with non-sensitive details for debugging
Implement graceful degradation when optional API keys are missing
anti_patterns: Skipping validation and waiting for first API call to fail
Exposing actual API key values in error messages or logs
Using generic 'Invalid API key' messages without remediation guidance
examples: OpenAI API keys must start with 'sk-' prefix
AWS credentials should match IAM key format patterns
Validate key length and character sets before making requests

patterns.name: Validate Framework-Specific Project Structure
patterns.description: Verify framework-specific directory structures and conventions before build or runtime. For Next.js 14, ensure 'app/' directory exists (not 'pages/'), proper Server/Client Component separation, and correct route file naming.
best_practices: Create pre-build validation scripts that check directory structure
Document required directory conventions in project README
Use framework CLI tools for project initialization to ensure correct structure
Implement build-time checks that fail fast with helpful error messages
Validate both structure and file naming conventions (e.g., page.tsx, layout.tsx)
anti_patterns: Mixing app/ and pages/ directories in Next.js 13+
Creating custom directory structures that conflict with framework expectations
Ignoring framework migration guides when upgrading major versions
examples: Next.js 14: app/page.tsx for routes, not pages/index.tsx
React: public/ for static assets, src/ for components
Vue 3: src/views/ for pages, src/components/ for reusable components

patterns.name: Three-Tier Caching for API Cost Optimization
patterns.description: Implement multi-level caching strategy to minimize external API costs. Tier 1 (build-time static generation), Tier 2 (client-side IndexedDB), and Tier 3 (server-side key-value store) work together to serve content with minimal API calls.
best_practices: Generate static content at build time for predictable data
Use IndexedDB or LocalStorage for client-side caching with TTL
Implement server-side deduplication using Redis or Vercel KV
Set appropriate cache expiration policies per tier (static: forever, client: 7 days, server: 30 days)
Monitor cache hit rates and API costs to validate effectiveness
Include cache metadata (source, timestamp) in responses for debugging
anti_patterns: Relying solely on server-side caching without client optimization
Setting cache TTLs too short, negating cost benefits
Caching sensitive or user-specific data in shared tiers
Ignoring cache invalidation strategies when source data changes
examples: Pre-generate AI content for 169 patterns at build time (Tier 1)
Cache API responses in IndexedDB with 7-day expiration (Tier 2)
Deduplicate identical prompts across users with Vercel KV (Tier 3)

patterns.name: AI Content Validation Pipeline
patterns.description: Implement automated validation to prevent AI hallucination and ensure factual accuracy. Cross-reference all AI-generated content with authoritative source data using rule-based and statistical checks.
best_practices: Define validation rules based on source data schema and domain requirements
Implement automated checks for factual accuracy (e.g., matching key terms from source)
Use statistical validation (e.g., sentence similarity scores) to detect drift
Create manual review workflows for flagged content
Log validation results for continuous improvement
Implement fallback to template-based content when validation fails
anti_patterns: Trusting AI-generated content without validation
Using overly strict validation that flags correct content as errors
Skipping validation for 'simple' content generation tasks
Failing to provide human review mechanisms for edge cases
examples: Validate quiz questions mention at least 2 best practices from source pattern
Check scenario outcomes reference specific anti-patterns from source data
Ensure generated images don't contain hallucinated Workday UI elements

patterns.name: Mobile-First Responsive Design
patterns.description: Design and develop interfaces starting with mobile constraints (375px width), progressively enhancing for larger screens. Ensures usability across all devices with appropriate touch targets and layout adaptations.
best_practices: Start CSS with mobile styles, add breakpoints for tablet/desktop
Use min-width media queries for progressive enhancement
Ensure touch targets are minimum 44x44px for mobile accessibility
Test interactive components on actual mobile devices, not just browser emulation
Implement responsive typography using clamp() or fluid scales
Optimize images with srcset for different screen densities
anti_patterns: Designing desktop-first and trying to 'squeeze' content onto mobile
Using hover-only interactions without touch alternatives
Setting touch targets smaller than 44px
Relying solely on browser dev tools for mobile testing
examples: Quiz buttons: 48px height with 12px padding on mobile
Responsive navigation: hamburger menu on mobile, full navbar on desktop
Card layouts: single column on mobile, grid on tablet/desktop

patterns.name: Test-Driven Development with E2E Coverage
patterns.description: Implement comprehensive testing strategy with unit tests (80%+ coverage), integration tests (90%+ coverage), and end-to-end tests for critical user flows. Ensures reliability and prevents regressions.
best_practices: Write unit tests for pure functions and business logic
Use integration tests for API routes and database interactions
Implement E2E tests with Playwright or Cypress for critical user journeys
Mock external APIs (e.g., OpenAI) in tests using MSW or similar
Run tests in CI/CD pipeline before deployment
Test error scenarios and edge cases, not just happy paths
Measure and maintain coverage thresholds
anti_patterns: Writing tests after implementation (missing edge cases)
Testing implementation details instead of behavior
Skipping E2E tests because they're 'slow'
Using production APIs in test suites
examples: Unit test: Pattern parser correctly filters by category
Integration test: /api/generate/quiz returns valid quiz structure
E2E test: User completes quiz, sees score, progress persists after refresh

patterns.name: WCAG 2.1 AA Accessibility Compliance
patterns.description: Ensure web application meets WCAG 2.1 Level AA standards for accessibility. Includes keyboard navigation, screen reader support, sufficient color contrast, and semantic HTML.
best_practices: Use semantic HTML elements (button, nav, main, article) for proper structure
Ensure all interactive elements are keyboard accessible (Tab, Enter, Space)
Provide ARIA labels and descriptions for screen readers
Maintain color contrast ratio of 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for UI components
Test with screen readers (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver)
Include skip-to-content links for keyboard users
Ensure focus indicators are visible and high-contrast
anti_patterns: Using div/span with onClick instead of button elements
Relying solely on color to convey information
Removing focus outlines without providing alternatives
Creating keyboard traps in modal dialogs or dropdowns
examples: Quiz options: <button> elements with aria-pressed state
Progress dashboard: aria-live regions for dynamic updates
Navigation: skip link to main content for keyboard users

patterns.name: Graceful Error Handling with User Feedback
patterns.description: Implement comprehensive error handling that provides clear user feedback, logs errors for debugging, and degrades gracefully when services fail.
best_practices: Catch and handle errors at appropriate boundaries (API routes, component boundaries)
Provide user-friendly error messages without exposing technical details
Log errors with context (user action, request ID, timestamp) for debugging
Implement retry logic with exponential backoff for transient failures
Use React Error Boundaries to prevent full application crashes
Provide fallback UI when components fail to render
anti_patterns: Showing technical stack traces to end users
Swallowing errors silently without logging
Using generic 'Something went wrong' messages without guidance
Failing to implement retry logic for known transient errors
examples: OpenAI rate limit: retry after delay, show 'Generating content...' message
Network failure: show cached content with banner 'Showing offline version'
Component error: Error Boundary shows 'Unable to load this section' with refresh button

patterns.name: API Cost Tracking and Budget Alerts
patterns.description: Monitor external API usage and costs with automated budget alerts. Track token consumption, estimate costs per operation, and trigger warnings before exceeding budgets.
best_practices: Log every API call with token counts and cost estimation
Calculate costs using current API pricing (e.g., GPT-4o: $5/1M input tokens)
Set daily and monthly budget thresholds with alert mechanisms
Aggregate costs by operation type (quiz generation, scenarios, hints)
Create dashboard for cost analysis and optimization opportunities
Implement rate limiting when approaching budget thresholds
anti_patterns: Discovering high costs only when bill arrives
Estimating costs without tracking actual token usage
Setting unrealistic budgets that break features when exceeded
Failing to differentiate between essential and optional API calls
examples: Log: 'Quiz generation: 1,234 tokens, est. $0.006, cache hit: false'
Alert: 'Daily budget 80% consumed, consider enabling aggressive caching'
Dashboard: 'This month: $8.42 / $10.00 budget, 842 API calls, 68% cache hit rate'

patterns.name: Progressive Enhancement for Core Functionality
patterns.description: Ensure core functionality works without JavaScript, progressively enhancing with interactive features. Provides baseline usability for all users regardless of browser capabilities or network conditions.
best_practices: Render critical content on server (SSR/SSG) for no-JS scenarios
Use form submissions for core actions, enhance with JavaScript
Provide noscript fallbacks for JavaScript-dependent features
Test application with JavaScript disabled to verify core functionality
Use semantic HTML that works without CSS or JavaScript
Lazy load non-critical JavaScript to improve initial load time
anti_patterns: Building SPAs that show blank page without JavaScript
Relying on client-side routing without server-side fallbacks
Requiring JavaScript for content that could be server-rendered
Ignoring users with JavaScript disabled or outdated browsers
examples: Pattern browsing: Server-rendered list works without JS, filters enhanced with JS
Quiz: Form submission works without JS, instant feedback requires JS
Navigation: HTML links work, client-side routing enhances experience
